scripts.//test: The suite is TypeScript, and the Worker has no build step, so it runs on node's own type stripping rather than a test framework. Without the flag every file fails to load on Node < 22.18 — which is how 119 passing tests went unnoticed as 7 failures.
scripts.test: npm run typecheck && npm run contracts && node --experimental-strip-types --test test/*.test.ts
scripts.//typecheck: Nothing else in this pipeline type-checks: wrangler bundles with esbuild and the suite runs on node's type-stripping, both of which ERASE types without reading them. A `const` read above its own declaration therefore shipped and silently disabled the server's ground witness. `test` runs this first so it cannot happen again.
scripts.//contracts: Swift talks to this Worker talks to Postgres, and those seams match by NAME at runtime and by nothing before it. A field the Worker stops emitting just becomes nil on the lock screen; a column that isn't there is a 400 the caller's catch eats.
